subject: general
question: In March 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi inaugurated 'Vantara' in Jamnagar, Gujarat. What is the primary purpose of this facility?

options.text: To act as an advanced animal rescue, conservation and rehabilitation centre
To serve as a luxury wildlife safari resort
To operate as an agricultural research institute for agricultural development
To function as a commercial zoo for tourism

solution:
The correct answer is option 1,"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• 'Vantara' is an advanced **animal rescue, conservation, and rehabilitation centre** inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi in Jamnagar, Gujarat.
 
• The facility is a dedicated effort to protect and rehabilitate **native and endangered wildlife species.**
 
• It focuses on providing advanced care and treatment to animals rescued from illegal trade, injury, or other distressing circumstances.
 
• The centre is part of the government's initiative to promote **environmental conservation and biodiversity preservation.**
 
• Vantara is expected to become a hub for scientific research related to wildlife conservation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

 
• **Wildlife Conservation:**

 
 
• Wildlife conservation refers to the practice of protecting animal species and their habitats to ensure biodiversity and ecological balance.
 
• Efforts include rescue centres, breeding programs, habitat restoration, and anti-poaching measures.
 
• India is home to several endangered species, including the Bengal tiger, Indian elephant, and Asiatic lion.
 
 
 
• **Endangered Species:**
 
 
• Endangered species are those at risk of extinction due to habitat loss, hunting, climate change, or other factors.
 
• Efforts to protect endangered species include national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, and conservation centres like Vantara.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity in India:**
 
 
• India is one of the 17 megadiverse countries in the world, housing around 8% of the global species diversity.
 
• Initiatives such as Project Tiger and Project Elephant aim to protect flagship species and their ecosystems.
 
 
 
• **Illegal Wildlife Trade:**
 
 
• Illegal wildlife trade poses a significant threat to biodiversity, involving species like pangolins, turtles, and exotic birds.
 
• Rescue centres like Vantara help rehabilitate animals seized from illegal trade operations.
